summary:
Bullpen is the category to lean on across every rating right now — R4's bullpen cell is running 95-66 (59%) over the last 14 days, with R1/R2/R3 all sitting at 91-70 (57%), well clear of their season baselines in the low-50s. Trends remains the steadiest anchor at 58% across all four ratings over the same window, and trends+sp (56.9%, n=576) and trends+runs (56.4%, n=637) remain the two combos to trust when they stack with a bullpen signal. The one soft spot is R4's starting pitcher category, flagged cold at -5.6pts off its 55% season mark — worth discounting SP-driven edges from R4 specifically, and R2's runs category is on a quiet 3-game losing streak worth watching before firing full units there.

Today's board gives six true four-way consensus plays, and BOS @ TBR is the one to prioritize: all four ratings stack TBR with rising confidence from R1 (+1.72) up to R3 (+1.98), and TBR is 70% (38-16) on the season when picked, 73% and +21.0u in strong-play spots — exactly the profile that pairs with the hot bullpen trend given Ranger Suarez making a road bullpen-taxing start. ATH @ CLE is the other clean stack, with all four ratings clustering tightly around +2.1 to +2.6 on CLE, the widest average delta on the slate — strong consensus signal size matters here since these ratings hit 61-65% in 30-day strong-play windows. ATL @ HOU and DET @ CHW both show full consensus fading the home side (ATL road pick, DET road fade), letting the trends+runs combo do its work on two separate boards. Fade the split games — CHC @ CIN, MIL @ BAL, KCR @ PIT, SFG @ LAD, PHI @ NYM — where R4 disagrees with the pack on four of five; given R4's own SP category is currently cold, its dissent in KCR @ PIT (leaning PIT while R1 likes KCR) should tilt weight back toward the R1-R3 consensus rather than R4's outlier call.
